$comment: MACHINE half of GET /wire and GET /wire/<source>; the HUMAN half is wire.md. GW-WIRE-VIEW owns `index_output` (and `member_headers`, the provenance of one member — its body is the stored bytes, not JSON of this schema) and the error code; GW-WIRE-RECORD owns `$defs.provenance` (what a record says about itself). `sha256` is the digest of the answer as the vendor sent it: for a `public` record also the digest of the stored bytes, for an `account` record the answer's identity only (the stored bytes are the sanitised structure). A source with no good answer yet is not listed as a member (404); in the index it carries null `fetched_at`/`age_s`/`complete` and its `last_error`.

wire_declarations.$comment: The declarations file GATEWAY_WIRE names (GW-WIRE-PROBE): the ONE home of a probe and of the account class's key allowlist — never the policy (a `wire` key there refuses the load), never code. No file, or an empty one, declares nothing. `_`-prefixed keys are comments.

probes.description: source name -> one GET on a declared rail's upstream, read through the rail's own credential lifecycle and recorded as an `account` source

rail.description: a rail the policy declares (today: codex)

path.description: a path on the rail's upstream — no host, no query, never an inference path

keep_keys.description: account source -> the keys whose string values are kept verbatim (every other string becomes its length); never an identity key, and a credential-shaped value is still withheld

source.description: the source name a vendor read registered

url.description: the URL the read went to (no credential: none rides in a URL the gateway builds)

status.description: the HTTP status of the kept answer; null = no good answer yet

fetched_at.description: when the kept answer was received

complete.description: false = the answer was cut at the bound

last_error.description: the latest failed read beside the kept answer: `status <n>`, `unreachable`, `withheld`, `over-bound`

wire-not-recorded.description: no good answer is recorded for this source (never read, or every read failed)
